title: Defining Your First Model
description: Create a simple model with fields and learn about common field types.

slides.title: A Simple Blog Post Model
slides.codeSnippet:
from django.db import models

class Post(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    content = models.TextField()
    published_date = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

slides.title: Field Types Explained 🔍
slides.content:
## Common Field Types

- **`CharField`** – For short text strings. `max_length` is required.
- **`TextField`** – For long text, no length limit.
- **`IntegerField`** – For integers.
- **`BooleanField`** – True/False.
- **`DateTimeField`** – Date and time.
- **`EmailField`** – Validates email format.
- **`URLField`** – Validates URL.

You also pass **options** like:
- `null=True` – allow database NULL.
- `blank=True` – allow empty string in forms.
- `default` – default value.
- `unique` – must be unique across rows.

quizData.question: Which field would you use to store a blog post's content that can be very long?
quizData.explanation: TextField is for unbounded text. CharField is for short strings with a max_length.

slides.title: Adding Options to Fields
slides.codeSnippet:
class Post(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200, unique=True)
    content = models.TextField(blank=True)  # allows empty in forms
    likes = models.IntegerField(default=0)
    is_published = models.BooleanField(default=False)

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Always import `models` from `django.db`

All model fields live under `models`. So you always start with `from django.db import models`.
